page: Microsoft Azure E4ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The CPU architecture is arm64, configured with 1 thread per core, 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a large 128 MB L3 cache. This instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data reveals a strong memory subsystem, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 454.17 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 87.86 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks. Single-threaded gzip compression performs strongly in the top 25% at 33.04 GB/sec. However, CPU-bound tasks show some limitations. The PassMark CPU score falls in the bottom 25%, and the CPU encryption test registers in the bottom 10% at 750.01, reflecting the lack of advanced vector and matrix extensions. Ray tracing performance is also weak, scoring 5482.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ps_v6 offers a high-density memory profile on an ARM architecture, which typically translates to lower power consumption and better resource-to-cost ratios for memory-bound workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Given the 32.0 GB memory capacity and average database operation performance (5034.94 on PassMark), this server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers such as Redis (achieving 8.3 million SET operations per second), static web serving, and lightweight database workloads.
